package_info.package_manager: source (C++ library, used in OpenSAML/Shibboleth, included in proprietary Ivanti products)
package_info.why_malicious: The package contains a critical Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) vulnerability (CVE-2023-36661) that allows attackers to supply malicious XML input. When the library processes this input, it resolves attacker-controlled URIs, enabling unauthorized access to internal resources, potential data exfiltration, denial of service, or, when chained with other vulnerabilities, unauthenticated remote code execution in products embedding the library.

execution_context.trigger: At runtime, during SAML/XML input processing
execution_context.file_location: Core xmltooling library (C++), within SAML/XML parsing routines handling KeyInfo elements

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when the application parses attacker-supplied SAML/XML input, the library processes the KeyInfo element and resolves the URI specified in the RetrievalMethod, causing the server to initiate an outbound HTTP request to an attacker-controlled or internal resource, resulting in unauthorized network access or data exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Allowing untrusted XML input to control URI resolution enables attackers to trigger arbitrary outbound network requests from the server, a hallmark of SSRF attacks. This can be leveraged to access internal-only services, exfiltrate sensitive data, or escalate to further compromise.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal SAML/XML processing should restrict URI resolution to trusted, pre-configured sources. Accepting and resolving arbitrary URIs from untrusted user input violates the principle of least privilege and exposes the server to SSRF risks.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate SAML implementations may fetch cryptographic keys from trusted, static URIs defined by administrators, but should never resolve URIs directly from user-supplied or unvalidated XML input.
key_indicators: Unvalidated URI resolution from user-controlled XML input
Outbound network requests initiated during SAML/XML parsing
No enforcement of URI scheme or destination restrictions in RetrievalMethod processing
Presence of <KeyInfo><RetrievalMethod URI=...> in authentication-related XML

attack_chain.action: Attacker submits a crafted SAML/XML document containing a KeyInfo element with a RetrievalMethod URI pointing to an attacker-controlled or internal resource.
attack_chain.leads_to: The vulnerable xmltooling library processes the XML and makes a server-side request to the specified URI, allowing the attacker to control the destination of the outbound request.

attack_chain.action: The server-side request can access internal resources (SSRF), exfiltrate data to the attacker, or be chained with other vulnerabilities (such as command injection) for further compromise.
attack_chain.leads_to: Potential denial of service, data exfiltration, or unauthenticated remote code execution, depending on the attacker's objectives and the environment.

behavioral_signatures: Unexpected outbound HTTP/HTTPS requests originating from SAML/XML processing components
Resolution of URIs directly from untrusted XML input during authentication workflows
Access to internal network resources triggered by parsing of KeyInfo/RetrievalMethod elements
file_indicators: SAML/XML files containing <KeyInfo><RetrievalMethod URI=...></KeyInfo> elements with external or internal URIs
Application or security logs showing URI resolution events during SAML authentication or XML parsing
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP/HTTPS requests from authentication or SAML-processing services to attacker-controlled domains
Unexpected HTTP/HTTPS requests to internal IP addresses or sensitive endpoints during SAML/XML authentication events
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor SAML/XML processing services for outbound network requests, especially those triggered during authentication or XML parsing. Inspect logs for KeyInfo/RetrievalMethod elements with non-whitelisted URIs. Use network monitoring to detect and alert on HTTP/HTTPS requests from authentication infrastructure to untrusted or internal destinations, and correlate these events with SAML/XML processing activity.
